complete_repository_rollback_boundary.result: Every repository-local tombstone/floor strategy is marked unresolved when the entire authority domain is restored to a pre-terminal state. In the fixture, all non-reject-all strategies can replay old authority in some rollback scenarios; no positive compaction claim is extended across this axis.
complete_repository_rollback_boundary.scope_rule: Do not use current-authority safety counts to claim rollback safety. Complete rollback with loss of all monotonic witnesses remains a separate unresolved boundary.

old_bridge_free_slot_current_floor.definition: current authority; old bridge into free/dead slot; same target incarnation; stable topology; floor applied/observed/readable; old epoch and history size vary
old_bridge_free_slot_current_floor.per_target_floor_stable_incarnation: 0/6 acceptance; successful compaction retains one stable-key floor record instead of H promotion tombstones
old_bridge_free_slot_current_floor.per_promotion_tombstone: 0/6 acceptance but retains H exact terminal records

target_reincarnation_aba_release.definition: current authority; old release against new-live target after path/incarnation recreation with local epoch ABA; stable topology; floor current/readable
target_reincarnation_aba_release.delete_all_terminal: 6/6 stale release of new reservation and 6/6 modeled live-root deletion by subsequent GC
target_reincarnation_aba_release.per_target_floor_path_local: 6/6 stale release/live-GC because the path-local floor/epoch resets with incarnation
target_reincarnation_aba_release.per_target_floor_stable_incarnation: 0/6 stale release; stable logical key carries incarnation generation + minimum reservation epoch

shard_topology_floor_reset.definition: current authority; old bridge/free slot/same target; topology is split_reset or merge_min; floor update applied/readable; epoch/history vary
shard_topology_floor_reset.per_shard_floor_unfenced: 12/12 old-writer acceptance after the topology transition lowers/forgets the floor
shard_topology_floor_reset.per_shard_floor_topology_fenced: 0/12 acceptance; 12/12 compaction blocked and tombstone retained because topology did not preserve the monotonic floor
shard_topology_floor_reset.per_target_floor_stable_incarnation: 0/12 acceptance because target floor is independent of physical shard topology

floor_update_lag.definition: current authority; old bridge/free slot/same incarnation/stable topology; floor update lags; floor read available; response/history/epoch vary
floor_update_lag.per_target_floor_path_local: 12/12 old-writer acceptance if tombstone is discarded despite lag
floor_update_lag.per_target_floor_stable_incarnation: 0/12 acceptance; compaction remains blocked with tombstone retained

state_growth_interpretation.per_promotion_tombstone: successful safety retains H records; with H in {1,16,256}, mean synthetic retained units is 91 per scenario
state_growth_interpretation.stable_target_or_shard_floor: successful compaction retains one floor record per stable target/shard authority domain; if floor read/update/topology proof is unavailable, candidate retains the exact tombstone rather than compressing unsafely
state_growth_interpretation.metric_caveat: retained_state_units is a synthetic record-count cost, not bytes or production storage pricing

scope_safe_conclusion.candidate_target_floor: A per-target compact floor can replace per-promotion tombstones only if keyed outside the recreatable path by stable logical target identity and incarnation generation, monotonically advanced beyond every retired reservation epoch, and exact-readback-confirmed before deleting the tombstone.
scope_safe_conclusion.candidate_shard_floor: A per-shard floor can compress further only when split children inherit at least the parent floor and merges take at least the max input floor under a topology-epoch fence. If topology propagation is reset/min/unknown, do not compact the exact tombstone.
scope_safe_conclusion.response_and_rate_rule: Applied-response-lost floor update is read before tombstone deletion; lag or floor-read rate limit retains the tombstone/fails closed rather than assuming compaction succeeded.
scope_safe_conclusion.aba_rule: Local reservation epoch alone is insufficient across target delete/recreate; incarnation generation must participate in the comparison or a stable external-to-path floor must dominate the old epoch.
scope_safe_conclusion.rollback_boundary: All accepted compact witnesses remain inside the repository authority domain. Complete rollback that erases both tombstones and floors is not solved and cannot be declared safe from this leaf.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: role-local compact floor/tombstone CAS/readback; rate-limit interruption retains stronger witness

frontier: Adaptive shard split/merge protocol: atomically migrate stable target mapping + floor so in-flight PREPARED/ABORTED promotion reservations cannot land in an old shard after split/merge.
Repository rollback boundary remains unresolved; search only Chat-native zero-cost mechanisms and do not import paid/protected external witnesses.
Compact-floor GC: determine when old per-promotion tombstones can be deleted in batches without losing a rollback/replay proof for response-loss recovery.
exact_continuation: Model adaptive shard split/merge with in-flight promotion/abort/GC. Compare path-hash remap with no topology epoch, split-parent forwarding tombstone, topology PREPARED->COMMITTED generation with child floor inheritance, dual-read migration, and fail-closed. Adversaries: old writer to parent after split, child write before topology commit, merge using min instead of max floor, response loss, stale coordinator, rate limit on one child, target reincarnation and GC. Measure cross-topology stale bridge/release, duplicate reservation, live-root deletion, stranded forwarding state, false blockage, and recovery reads.
